Uber — key metrics pack from the desk series file. Latest print in file: FY2026Q3 (period end 2026-09-30).

Through the quarter ended September 30, 2026 · weekly marks through the week ending November 8, 2026

The business

Uber runs a marketplace app. Riders pay for trips, people order food and groceries, and shippers book trucks. Drivers, couriers and carriers do the work and keep most of what the customer pays. Uber's revenue is its cut of that spend, plus a few lines it books in full.

Mobility (rides) is the profit centre. Delivery is the second leg and the faster grower. Freight is a small trucking brokerage that still loses money. Operating income turned positive in 2023, and free cash flow has climbed every year since 2021.

Net income is the noisy line, because Uber marks its stakes in other companies to market every quarter. A year ago a one-off tax gain and investment gains lifted Q3 2025 earnings to $3.11 a share. This quarter an investment loss cut them to $0.25, even as operating income rose 30%. That swing is why trailing earnings fell from $4.55 to $1.69 and the trailing earnings multiple jumped to about 40×; the price barely moved.

Risks

  • Durability break: drivers and couriers reclassified as employees, or a price war in rides. Watch Mobility revenue growth, operating income, and free cash flow.
  • Big swings in net income and EPS from investment marks can hide the operating trend.
  • Robotaxi players could own the rider relationship in dense cities.
  • Freight stays a drag tied to the trucking cycle.

Close competitors

  • Lyft — the U.S. rides rival.
  • DoorDash — the delivery leader in the U.S.
  • Grab — rides and delivery across Southeast Asia, the market Uber sold to it.
  • Waymo — driverless rides, now a partner in some cities and a rival in others.

Valuation

Every complete week from the week ending Aug 2, 2020 to the week ending Nov 8, 2026 is on the axis. The multiple is blank for the week ending Aug 2, 2020 through the week ending Oct 1, 2023, because trailing earnings were not positive. From the week ending Oct 4, 2026 it divides by $1.69 of trailing earnings per share through September, so the jump to about 40× is last year's one-off tax and investment gain dropping out, not a price move. The last week's price is our own volume-weighted average of daily closes. There is no forward multiple because there is no sourced forward earnings estimate.

Open gaps

  • Diluted EPS, 2018. Not printed: the 2018 per-share line to common stockholders is a dash, because all 2018 earnings went to preferred dividends.
  • Income, shares and cash flow for 2017–2018, plus 2018 net income, Q4 2018, Q4 2020 revenue, Q4 2023 operating income, and Q4 and 2017–2019 segment revenue. Printed in the 10-Ks and Q4 earnings releases; we read them ourselves because our shared data store does not carry them yet.
  • Segment revenue for Mobility and Delivery in 2017, and every quarter before Q2 2020 except Q4 2019. 2017 is not printed (Uber reported Rides and Eats then); the early quarters are printed but not yet extracted.
  • Segment operating income before 2025, and Q4 2025. Uber adopted this measure in 2026 and recast only the first three quarters of 2025; earlier years used adjusted EBITDA, which is a different measure and is not spliced in.
  • Trailing EPS, Q1–Q3 2018. Not printed: four printed quarters are not available before Q4 2018.
  • Employees, and revenue and net income per employee, 2017–2018. Not printed: Uber filed no 10-K before its May 2019 listing.
  • Weekly multiples from the week ending Oct 4, 2026. Data hold: our shared weekly file still divides these weeks by June's trailing figures and has no price for the week ending Nov 8. We re-divided the same weekly prices by the September trailing figures, and priced the last week from public daily closes, until the shared file catches up.
  • Q3 2026 figures. Data hold: read straight from the Q3 10-Q and earnings release; our shared data store has not captured the Q3 print yet.
  • Forward earnings multiple. No sourced forward earnings estimate, so nothing is drawn.
  • Trips, Gross Bookings, monthly active consumers and adjusted EBITDA history. Printed in each earnings release but not yet extracted; the Q3 2026 prints are on the key-metrics board.
